correctness.rationale: The claim is a metric projection theorem on a closed convex set. Axial twirling is an orthogonal Hilbert--Schmidt projection and reduces every optimizer to the diagonal plane. The symmetric two-qubit PPT calculation gives the exact classical parabola. The weighted Euclidean projection to its upper boundary has derivative \(\tfrac12(3y^3+(6b-1)y-2x)\); physicality and nonclassicality prove the cubic has exactly one root in \((-1,1)\). The root-of-unity decomposition and rank argument prove coherent length three. `verify.py` replays all supplementary algebraic and numerical checks with `VERIFY_OK`.

originality.rationale: The primary mixed-state spin-1 paper computes general mixed quantumness numerically and states that its arbitrary-mixed proof is missing. Its analytic segment construction covers the diagonal ray \(x=0\), but not the off-axis two-parameter diagonal family. The 2011 geometry paper parameterizes the classical body rather than stating this Hilbert--Schmidt projection, while broader closest-separable-state papers optimize over the larger set of all separable two-qubit states.
residual_risks: The full body of arXiv:1110.0325 was not available through the successful text route; its abstract and targeted indexed searches did not expose a Hilbert--Schmidt projection theorem, but an equivalent diagonal calculation could be buried in the paper.
A later result may formulate the same projection as a Euclidean projection onto the axially symmetric classical slice without using spin-quantumness or closest-classical terminology.

The \(x=0\) nonclassical ray is prior-covered and is included only to state the natural complete diagonal theorem; originality rests on the off-axis two-parameter extension and structural optimizer classification.

value.rationale: Diagonal spin-1 mixtures are the natural axially invariant mixed states and are experimentally/basic-model relevant rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. The source treated general mixed quantumness numerically; the theorem gives a complete exact two-parameter solution on this symmetry class, a unique closest classical state, and the minimal number of coherent states needed to realize it. This supplies an analytic benchmark for mixed-state quantumness and isolates a nontrivial off-axis extension beyond the previously known Queen-of-Quantum segment.
